generation.raw_text: {"status":"answered","answer":"In a food chain, the amount of energy transferred from one step to the next decreases significantly. At each transfer, a large proportion of energy, about 80 to 90 percent, is lost as heat during processes like respiration. This means that only a small fraction of the energy is passed on to the next trophic level. As a result, after three steps in a food chain, very little energy is available for top carnivores to use. This is why food chains are typically short, consisting of only a few steps.","selected_evidence_ids":["E2"],"citations":[{"evidence_id":"E2","pdf_page":215,"textbook_page":206}],"missing_information":[]}
